definition: How many examples suffice to learn a hypothesis class to a given accuracy, and across 4 sources the formal axis on which the archive's theory papers characterise transformers. The results: the VC dimension of depth-L transformers with W parameters is O(LW log(TW)) with a nearly matching lower bound, so both the parameter dependence and the multiplicative logarithm in sequence length are tight; chain-of-thought learning by teacher forcing costs only logarithmically more as the number of reasoning steps grows; and separate treatments sharpen the generalisation picture and analyse internalising a chain of thought. Two boundaries the archive keeps. These bound what is learnable in principle, not what gradient descent finds. And they are proved for hard attention, deliberately, because softmax reintroduces the difficulties known from sigmoidal networks -- so they characterise a neighbouring architecture.

evidence.note: Compares two training-free intent classifiers built from summary statistics of prefill-time activations against trained heads on the same features, and finds the trade-off is not accuracy but where each fails — trained heads win fine-grained distinctions, statistical ones give better uncertainty on mixed prompts and survive adversarial rephrasing that collapses the trained heads to zero.
evidence.title: Training-Free versus Training-Based Intent Classification in LLMs: Accuracy, Robustness, and Failure Modes

evidence.note: Derives a non-vacuous PAC-Bayes generalization bound for transformers on boolean functions in terms of Fourier sparsity and degree, and uses it to show chain of thought turns an exponential dependence on reasoning length into a linear one for Parity.
evidence.title: A Sharper Picture of Generalization in Transformers

evidence.note: Pins down the VC dimension of transformers as depth times parameters times a logarithm, and shows chain-of-thought learning by teacher forcing costs only logarithmically more as the number of reasoning steps grows.
evidence.title: Tight Sample Complexity of Transformers

evidence.note: Proves that reasoning can be moved from emitted tokens into hidden states without losing sample efficiency, using a curriculum that deletes thinking tokens in geometric chunks and so needs only logarithmically many training stages.
evidence.title: Transformers Provably Learn to Internalize Chain-of-Thought

name: sample complexity
